newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish crown seen unmoved by any Italy ERM entry.
newsitem.headline: Swedish crown seen unmoved by any Italy ERM entry.

text.p: The Swedish crown is not likely to be significantly affected if the Italian lira re-enters the European exchange rate mechanism at the weekend, economists and money market dealers told Reuters on Friday.

"I really don't think you buy crowns on the possibility of a lira-ERM link. People are no longer assuming that the crown will go in if another currency does," said Peter Lindqvist, economist at HSBC Midland.
Many dealers however believed that a weaker German mark would benefit the Swedish unit in the short term.

"Probably the D-mark will be sold on a lira-ERM link and that can have a positive effect on the crown. At the same time there's a risk that the D-mark is already being traded down so there's a risk of a rebound on Monday," said one chief dealer.
Swedbank economists believe the parity of any lira link would be the key to market reaction.

"It's really important what level it goes in at. If it's an obviously weaker level, say 1,025-1,050 to the mark, we could get a negative reaction for the crown. If it's under 1,000 that would mean you have to enter at a tough level and could be positive for the crown," said Swedbank economist Knut Hallberg.
Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said earlier that Italy would ask for a return to the ERM by the end of November.
A senior banking source in Frankfurt told Reuters that Italy had sought a meeting of the European Union's monetary committee for Saturday.
By 1245 GMT, while the lira had firmed against the mark, the Swedish crown had also firmed to 4.4100-30 crowns per mark versus 4.4125 yesterday.
